statusText: Calm, wait-and-see conditions continue into the European late morning, roughly 35-45 minutes ahead of today's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales / 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich data cluster. Asia-Pacific closed broadly higher Friday (Nikkei 225 +0.75%, Topix +0.23%, Kospi +2.54%) tracking Thursday's Wall Street record close (S&P 500 +0.65% to 7,798.99; Nasdaq Composite +0.81% to 26,803.03), with regional chip names extending the sector's strength (SoftBank +5.08%, Tokyo Electron +2.13%, Advantest +4.02%, Kioxia +3.87%); Australia's ASX 200 was the lone laggard, -0.63%. U.S. equity futures are mixed heading into the cash open (S&P 500 futures roughly flat at +0.01%, Nasdaq 100 futures off about 0.15%) -- a modest but directionally coherent premarket print, unlike the prior run's internally inconsistent NQ quote. VIX holds flat-to-firm near 14.5-14.75 and the 10-year Treasury yield remains anchored near Thursday's 4.65% close (no fresher Friday print yet surfaced). Oil continues to firm on the unresolved Iran/Hormuz backdrop (WTI ~$81.3, Brent ~$87.9-88.0) after Iran's Foreign Minister again said Tehran is not engaged in direct talks with Washington and that the Strait will not fully reopen "until America corrects its behavior," even as the parallel Oman-brokered technical arrangement remains described as "very close" -- the same progress-in-talks/conditional posture as prior runs, not a new kinetic escalation. Alpha Vantage remained fully rate-limited on both the initial call and a retry (a tenth consecutive run), so this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch; evidence this run was more internally consistent across sources than the prior run's mismatched futures print, so Confidence ticks modestly higher.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Continue monitoring through the run-up to the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales and 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich sentiment cluster and the subsequent U.S. cash open; an upgrade to a higher Tail state still requires observed persistent one-way structure with failed pullbacks in the broad Nasdaq-100 complex itself, not the pending data cluster, the unresolved Hormuz/Iran rhetoric, the mixed premarket futures print, or this run's continued Alpha Vantage outage.

body: About 35-40 minutes past the top of the hour, conditions remain calm heading into the European late morning, roughly one hour on from the prior run. Asia-Pacific markets closed broadly higher on Friday, tracking Thursday's Wall Street record close (S&P 500 +0.65% to 7,798.99, Nasdaq Composite +0.81% to 26,803.03): Japan's Nikkei 225 added over 0.75% and the Topix rose 0.23%, South Korea's Kospi advanced 2.54% (Kosdaq +1.10%), while Australia's ASX 200 was the lone laggard, 0.63% lower. Regional chip names extended the sector's overnight strength, with SoftBank Group +5.08%, Tokyo Electron +2.13%, Advantest +4.02% and Kioxia +3.87%, consistent with Thursday's broad-based Nvidia/TSMC/Broadcom/SK Hynix/Micron/AMD premarket rally noted in the prior run. U.S. equity futures are mixed heading into the cash open: S&P 500 futures roughly flat (+0.01%) while Nasdaq 100 futures are off about 0.15%, a modest but directionally coherent print (unlike the prior run's internally inconsistent NQ quote, which mismatched last-price vs bid/ask levels). VIX holds flat-to-firm near 14.5-14.75 (little changed from the prior run's 14.4-14.8 range), and the 10-year Treasury yield remains anchored near Thursday's 4.65% close, with no fresher Friday print yet surfaced; Alpha Vantage TREASURY_YIELD was retried once and both attempts returned an immediate rate_limit error (a tenth consecutive run), so yields again come from WebSearch context rather than a fresh pull. Oil continues to firm on the unresolved Iran/Hormuz backdrop -- WTI near $81.3 and Brent near $87.9-88.0 -- after Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi again said Tehran is not engaged in direct talks with Washington and that the Strait will not fully reopen "until America corrects its behavior," even as the parallel Oman-brokered technical arrangement remains described as "very close." This is the same progress-in-talks/conditional posture identified in prior runs, not a new kinetic escalation, and no fresh attack or discontinuity was identified for this run specifically. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota remains exhausted for a tenth consecutive run, so per the fallback protocol this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch for yields, oil, VIX, equities and price-path context; however, this run's evidence was more internally consistent across sources (a coherent directional premarket futures read, corroborating Asia-session read-through, and a stable Hormuz characterization) than the prior run's mismatched futures print and blocked direct-fetch attempts, so Confidence ticks up modestly to 36 (still low, up from 34). Tail holds at 9% (still low; the modest premarket Nasdaq softness is a single data point, not observed persistent one-way structure with failed pullbacks in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself) while Stress firms slightly to 28% (moderate, up from 27%) on continued pre-event positioning, with the main forecast driver remaining the pending 12:30 UTC Retail Sales / 14:00 UTC UMich cluster, projected to push Stress toward the mid-40s around the release before easing back through the afternoon, evening, and into the quiet Saturday handover.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (9-18%) through the full prior 24 hours as the index ground to a fresh S&P 500 record above 7,800 on soft PPI; Stress ran elevated to high (up to 58%) around the Wednesday/Thursday CPI-PPI and AMAT-earnings window before easing back into the low-to-moderate band (23-29%) through Friday's European morning as the after-hours reaction stayed contained to single names and no broader transmission was confirmed.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (5-11%) through the next 24 hours; Stress is projected to build from the high-20s toward the mid-40s across the 12:30-14:00 UTC Retail Sales / UMich sentiment cluster and the U.S. cash-open/power-hour window before easing back through the evening and into the quiet Saturday handover, with no forecast slot currently implying an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to stay in the low-to-medium-low band throughout, reflecting the continued Alpha Vantage outage, though this run's more internally consistent WebSearch evidence supports a modestly higher starting point than the prior run.

forecastDetail.comment: European late morning holds calm heading into the U.S. data cluster; Asia closed broadly higher on chip-sector strength (Nikkei +0.75%, Kospi +2.54%, SoftBank +5.08%, Tokyo Electron +2.13%, Advantest +4.02%, Kioxia +3.87%) while U.S. futures are mixed into the cash open (S&P 500 roughly flat, Nasdaq 100 off ~0.15%); VIX holds flat-to-firm near 14.5-14.75 and Iran again says it is not in direct talks with Washington even as the parallel Oman technical arrangement stays "very close" -- an unchanged progress-in-talks posture, no new kinetic escalation identified this run.

Final hour before the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print; Stress continues to build on forecast dispersion and pre-event positioning while Tail stays anchored in the low band absent any observed persistent one-way structure in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself.

U.S. Retail Sales (July, 8:30am ET) prints within this hour -- consensus +0.3% MoM headline, +0.2% ex-auto -- the session's first major checkpoint; Stress rises toward the elevated band on event/whipsaw risk while Tail requires an observed failed-pullback/persistent-extension reaction before it could follow, which is not yet asserted.

University of Michigan preliminary consumer sentiment (August, 10am ET; consensus 54.1 vs 55.2 prior) prints within this hour on the heels of Retail Sales, keeping the window in event/whipsaw mode; Stress is projected to peak here before easing through the afternoon as the data cluster clears.

Data cluster has fully cleared and the U.S. cash open (9:30am ET) falls within this hour; Stress begins easing back toward the moderate band into the power-hour window, with Tail unchanged absent confirmed persistent one-way structure.

Early U.S. session continuation window; Stress continues to ease as the morning data cluster and cash-open transition clear without a confirmed directional break, with dominant mode shifting back toward mixed/range conditions.
